name: Mitra-v2
developer: Amazon (AutoGluon team; Tao, Zhang, Liu, Han, Maddix, Fang, Han, Gai, Liu, Bohlke-Schneider, Wang, Friedland, Mah, Lee, Kong)

availability.notes: Classifier and regressor checkpoints (safetensors + config.json) on Hugging Face (autogluon/mitra-classifier-2, autogluon/mitra-regressor-2; regressor at https://huggingface.co/autogluon/mitra-regressor-2). Inference + fine-tuning code and the per-unit TabArena evaluation results are released as the mitra-finetune package (installed from the HF git repo, not on PyPI; needs autogluon.tabular[mitra]>=1.6, tabarena>=0.1.0, Python 3.11-3.13 and a CUDA GPU; flash-attn optional). The weights are also a drop-in replacement inside AutoGluon via hyperparameters={'MITRA': {'hf_model': 'autogluon/mitra-classifier-2'}} (AutoGluon's stock MITRA defaults still load the v1 checkpoints autogluon/mitra-classifier / -regressor, and its stock fine-tuning defaults differ from the paper recipe). TabArena ships its own wrapper (pip install tabarena[mitra_v2]). The pretraining pipeline (multi-node trainer, synthetic-data generators incl. the Hybrid SCM implementation, and their configurations) is explicitly not released (paper App. A.2). No hosted API known.

license.prior_or_data: not released (pretraining pipeline and synthetic-data generators are withheld; no license applies)
license.notes: Paper App. A.2: the public release (weights, inference/fine-tuning code, evaluation results) is 'all under the Apache-2.0 license'. Hugging Face metadata of both checkpoint repos and of mitra-finetune: license: apache-2.0; the model cards state 'This project is licensed under the Apache-2.0 License'; mitra-finetune ships the Apache-2.0 LICENSE text; AutoGluon (the inference engine) is Apache-2.0. Apache-2.0 permits commercial and non-commercial use, modification and redistribution with notice/attribution retention. TabArena's method metadata declares license='Apache-2.0' and the leaderboard does not flag Mitra-v2 as non-commercial (unlike TabPFN-3.5, LimiX-2, TabFM, EXAONE).

architecture.type: element-wise 2D (row + column) attention transformer (Tab2D), in-context learner
architecture.parameters_note: 75.7M classifier / 76.7M regressor (the 1,000-bin regression head adds roughly one million parameters); paper rounds to 77M. Classifier is architecturally identical to Mitra-v1 (same count).
architecture.layers: 12 layers; each layer = attention across rows (examples) + FFN, then attention across columns (features) + FFN (FFN inner dim 2,048)
architecture.attention_scheme: Factorized 2D attention over cell tokens: in every layer attention is applied once across examples (row axis, within a feature) and once across features (column axis, within an example), each sublayer followed by its own feed-forward block. Query rows attend only to the support. No positional encoding, so predictions are invariant to row and column order. Plain dense softmax attention (prediction uses flash-attn varlen kernels when installed, fine-tuning uses PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention); no scalable-softmax / memory-efficient variants.
architecture.checkpoints: separate classification & regression (identical backbone; differ only in label embedding and output head: 10 class logits vs 1,000 bins)
architecture.regression_head: distributional, 1,000 bins (cross-entropy over bins on a fixed grid linspace(-0.5,1.5,1001) in the training fold's normalized target space; point prediction = mean of the predicted bin distribution; full histogram exposed via predict_distribution for CDF/PDF/quantiles/CRPS)
architecture.feature_embedding: Each scalar cell value is embedded independently to the 512-d hidden size (cell-as-token); support labels are embedded and added to their rows; query positions get a learned mask token; regression support targets are embedded by their bin. Inputs pass a per-support-set preprocessor (fit on the support, applied to the queries): mean imputation of NaNs, ordinal encoding of categoricals, optional quantile transformer (disabled in the released pretraining run), random mirroring of numerical axes / regression targets.
key_innovations: 10x longer pretraining context: 160-5,120 support rows and 1,280 query rows (Mitra-v1: <=512 support, 128 query)

New Hybrid SCM prior (35% of the outer mixture): random MLP, decision-tree, ExtraTrees, random-forest, 1D-convolution, GP (random Fourier features) and vector-autoregression mechanisms composed inside one causal DAG with vector-valued nodes
1,000-bin distributional regression head trained with cross-entropy, replacing v1's single-output MSE head (calibrated predictive distributions, CRPS/quantiles)
Geometry-aware composite optimizer: Muon on 2-D weight matrices + AdamW elsewhere, cosine schedule, 4 nodes x 8 H200

Deployment-time wrappers reusing the frozen checkpoint: train-only feature reduction to a 256-feature budget, balanced hierarchical decomposition for >10 classes, 8-fold bagged 50-step fine-tuning with heldout-in-support, prediction-time support caps up to 32,768 rows and 16,384-row query chunks

capabilities.max_classes_note: Native head: <=10 classes (pretraining cap; config dim_output=10). More classes are handled without retraining by a balanced hierarchical decomposition (classes permuted under a fixed seed and split into g=min(ceil(C/10),10) groups; a root Mitra node routes, one leaf node per group predicts; recurses when C>100; per-bag-child seeds diversify the grouping), implemented in mitra-finetune (hierarchy.py). On TALENT's 12 >10-class datasets this wrapper ranks first in the whole pool. AutoGluon's stock MITRA wrapper and the TabArena wrapper declare max_classes=10 (TabArena has no >10-class dataset).
capabilities.max_features_note: Pretrained on 1-50 features. The released pipeline feeds up to 256 columns to the model directly and reduces wider tables to a 256-feature budget (classification: train-only SelectKBest / ANOVA-F top-256, dtype-gated to predominantly continuous tables; regression: train-only 256-component truncated SVD / PCA), so there is no hard upper limit (TabArena wrapper declares max_features=50,000; the 1,024-feature QSAR-TID-11 and hiva_agnostic run natively). Budget adjustable via MITRA_CLS_MAX_FEATURES / MITRA_REG_MAX_FEATURES. AutoGluon's stock MITRA wrapper (v1 defaults) declares max_features=500.
capabilities.max_samples_note: No hard limit: larger tables are handled by subsampling the in-context support (class-balanced on binary tasks) to 16,384 rows (fine-tuning, classification) / 20,480 (fine-tuning, regression) and 16,384 (prediction, binary) / 32,768 (prediction, multiclass and regression), inside 8-fold bagging. TabArena wrapper declares max_rows=1,000,000; Mitra-v2 ran natively on every TabArena dataset (up to ~100k training rows). AutoGluon's stock MITRA wrapper declares max_rows=10,000 (tutorial: 'strongest on small tabular datasets' with <5,000 samples).
capabilities.categorical_features: Ordinal/label encoding in AutoGluon's Mitra preprocessor (OrdinalEncoder, unknown -> NaN -> mean-imputed); the synthetic prior converts a subset of continuous features to categorical in every generated dataset. One-hot expansion was tried at deployment and hurt (App. C).
capabilities.other: Missing values: mean imputation per support set (remaining NaN set to 0) in the Mitra preprocessor; no native missingness token. Distributional regression outputs (per-child histograms over 1,000 bins; exact mean/CDF/PDF/quantile/CRPS/log-score via RegressionDistribution). Fine-tuning and bagging built in. No multi-target, embeddings or text support.

pretraining.synthetic_prior_summary: Synthetic tasks generated online. For each task one generator is drawn from a hand-set 'outer' categorical mixture (Table 2): base TabPFN-style SCM 0.35, Hybrid SCM 0.35, decision tree 0.06, ExtraTrees 0.06, gradient boosting 0.06, random forest 0.06, directly sampled random forest 0.06 (the two causal generators hold 70% of the mass). Hybrid SCM = variant of the O-prior Hybrid Structural Causal Model (Bouadi et al. 2026): a random DAG with 3-7 nodes (chain parents plus earlier nodes added as skip-connection parents with probability 0.4), vector-valued nodes with independently sampled output dimensionality (O-prior uses scalar nodes); each non-root node applies a randomly selected mechanism (random MLP, decision tree, ExtraTrees, random forest, 1D convolution, Gaussian process via random Fourier features, vector autoregression) to the concatenation of its parents' outputs, and, with several parents, also independent random linear projections of each parent, aggregated by a random operator (mean, softmax-weighted sum, MLP projection, elementwise product, maximum) giving residual-like paths; per-node standardization with random feature-importance scaling and L2 normalization; features and target selected from the node outputs by k-means, farthest-point sampling or random selection; classification targets quantile-bucketed into class labels; a subset of continuous features converted to categorical in all datasets. Task shapes: 160-5,120 support rows (sampled uniformly), 1,280 query rows, 1-50 features, <=10 classes, numerical + synthesized categorical features; class and feature order shuffled, numerical axes randomly mirrored; optional quantile transformer and feature-count scaling disabled. Mixture weights are manual, not learned; reweighting them or log-uniform row sampling changed downstream accuracy little (App. C).
synthetic_prior_types: Hybrid SCM (O-prior variant: MLP / tree / ExtraTrees / random-forest / 1D-conv / GP-RFF / VAR mechanisms in one DAG)
pretraining.num_synthetic_datasets_note: About 28.7 million 'nominal' synthetic tasks for the classifier (~14,000 updates x 2,048 tasks) and about 34.8 million for the regressor (~17,000 updates incl. the 3,000-step fine-tune); 'nominal' because an exact count would depend on training-time metadata that was not fully logged. Mitra-v1: 45M nominal tasks.
pretraining.objective: Cross-entropy on the masked query labels given the support set (Eq. 1), i.e. -sum_j log p(y_q,j | X_s, y_s, X_q); regression uses the same loss over 1,000 target bins
pretraining.optimizer: Muon (Gram Newton-Schulz implementation, Dao 2026) on all 2-D weight matrices except the prediction head + AdamW for the remaining parameters; base learning rate 8e-4, cosine decay with 500 warm-up steps, maximum gradient norm 10, bfloat16 autocast
pretraining.training_steps: about 14,000 optimizer updates for the released classifier checkpoint; regressor: about 14,000 + 3,000 further fine-tuning steps (Mitra-v1: 22,000 steps)
pretraining.batch_size: 2,048 tasks per update (4 tasks per GPU per microbatch x 32 ranks x 16 gradient-accumulation microbatches)
pretraining.hardware: 4 nodes x 8 H200 GPUs (32 distributed ranks), bfloat16 autocast (Mitra-v1: 8x A100 40GB)
pretraining.compute: not reported: 'Accelerator hours, energy, and the realized prior mixture frequencies are ... not recoverable from the current metadata' (Sec. 5)
pretraining.training_cost_note: No GPU-hours, wall-clock or cost figure is published. Checkpoint quality was not monotonic in training steps, and continued/longer pretraining did not help (App. C); App. F reports an LLMZero-guided search of continuation trajectories that found a 750-step continuation worth +17.1 validation Elo on an independent run. The classification and regression checkpoints come from separate pretraining runs with the same recipe.
pretraining.curriculum: None stated. Support size sampled uniformly over 160-5,120 rows (log-uniform tried, little difference); no context-length or feature-count curriculum; synthetic tables generated online.

icl.context_note: Pretraining context: 160-5,120 support + 1,280 query rows (10x Mitra-v1's 512 + 128). Released deployment caps (frozen mitra-finetune defaults, overridable via MITRA_SUPPORT_CAP / MITRA_PREDICT_SUPPORT_CAP / MITRA_SUPPORT_SELECT): fine-tuning sees <=16,384 support rows (classification) / <=20,480 (regression); prediction conditions on <=16,384 rows on binary tasks (a time-budget choice) and <=32,768 on multiclass and regression, class-balanced on binary. No positional encoding and no architectural hard limit, but App. C reports that raising the classification support cap well past the released value (with exact chunked attention, so memory was not the limit) reduced accuracy: the model cannot exploit support sets much longer than those it was fine-tuned on. Support-cap sweep 512 -> 32,768 cut error by 28% (classification) / 21% (regression) in geometric mean on the largest datasets; cap 8,192 already realises 94% / 92% of that gain; two of the three largest tables were still improving at 32,768 (support-limited, not capacity-limited).
icl.large_dataset_strategy: Random subsampling of training rows to the support cap (class-balanced on binary), drawn once per test set when the support fits and freshly per 16,384-row query chunk when it is capped, inside 8-fold AutoGluon bagging: each bag child fine-tunes on its fit fold and then predicts with fit fold + its own held-out fold as in-context support ('heldout in support'; no refit; worth about 11 Elo on the regression board). Under CUDA OOM the query chunk is shrunk first (to 256 rows / stock 1,024), then the support cap halved (automatic halving ratchet); later bag children start at the context the first child settled on. Optional support cache (MITRA_SUPPORT_CACHE=1) encodes the support once per predict call (~5x faster multi-chunk prediction, exact). Wide tables reduced train-only to 256 features; >10 classes via hierarchical decomposition.
icl.test_time_ensembling: Default deployment = 8-fold AutoGluon bagging of independently fine-tuned children (class probabilities averaged; regression = equal-weight mixture of the children's 1,000-bin histograms, point prediction = mixture mean). One Mitra estimator per fold (n_estimators=1); no feature/class-permutation ensembling by default (AutoGluon's shuffle_classes / shuffle_features default False). The recipe is frozen; no per-dataset selection or HPO (TabArena: can_hpo=False).
icl.fine_tuning: Yes, and it is the default deployment mode ('default' on leaderboards = fine-tuned + bagged, not zero-shot). mitra-finetune recipe: 50-step full fine-tune per bag child with AdamW, lr 1e-5 (3e-6 on binary tasks whose training table has <=16,384 rows), 10 warm-up steps, weight decay 0.3, validation on the held-out fold with best-weights checkpointing (log_loss / RMSE; reported binary tasks used roc_auc), 250 s fine-tuning budget per child under TabArena's 1 h protocol (default time_limit 3,600 s per fit; on the largest tables only 11-30 of the 50 steps fit the budget). In AutoGluon: hyperparameters={'MITRA': {'fine_tune': True|False, 'fine_tune_steps': N, 'hf_model': 'autogluon/mitra-classifier-2'}}; stock AutoGluon defaults (fine_tune=True, fine_tune_steps=50, n_estimators=1, max_samples_support=8,192, max_samples_query=1,024, no heldout-in-support) differ from the paper recipe. Zero-shot inference (fine_tune=False) is supported but no zero-shot Mitra-v2 results are published ('a dedicated low-cost preset ... is future work').
icl.inference_notes: Requires a CUDA GPU for the recipe (AutoGluon can run in-context inference on CPU, 12-63x slower; CPU fine-tuning 'very slow'). Prediction in 16,384-row query chunks (stock AutoGluon 1,024 with a support redraw per chunk): bit-identical when the support fits, same in expectation otherwise, 5.2x lower total prediction time over TabArena and 7x on capped tables (APSFailure 1,419 s -> 185 s per split). Regression returns the mean of the bin distribution; predict_distribution returns per-child histograms with exact CDF/quantile/CRPS. Prediction time is not instrumented separately in the release artifacts.

speed.hardware_note: Paper timings on a single H100 (support-cap sweep) and H100 release artifacts (0.3 h mean per TabArena classification dataset per evaluation unit, 1.4 h max on APSFailure). TabArena hosted runs: 1x RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB) per fit; 108 GPU-hours measured fit + inference for all 816 splits (2026-09-12 run). Per-1K-row fit/inference times come from the TabArena leaderboard join.
speed.memory_note: The 2D layout has large, shape-changing activations; the wrappers enable expandable CUDA allocator segments and an OOM ratchet (query chunk, then support cap halved; a preflight forward/backward pass fails fast when the fine-tuning context does not fit). Flash-attn at prediction 'is faster and needs far less memory'. Distributional regression output ~32 KB per test row with eight children. AutoGluon's Mitra memory estimators scale quadratically in rows x features for large tables. Recorded OOM retries on the wide TabArena tables (Bioresponse, hiva_agnostic, kddcup09_appetency, QSAR-TID-11) all recovered.
speed.speed_claims: Median end-to-end evaluation unit (8-fold bagged fine-tune + prediction) about 8.8 min for classification and 9.6 min for regression on TabArena, versus seconds for forward-pass models (EXAONE Tabular, TabPFN-3) and 2-3 min for TabFM; fine-tuning dominates. Raising the prediction cap 8,192 -> 32,768 adds +25% (classification, worst +41%) / +9% (regression, worst +22%) end-to-end time, all prediction. The paper states the system 'is much slower than forward-pass foundation models and should not be described as zero-shot or Pareto-dominant', but no entry that spends more per dataset rates higher. Fine-tuning loop on SDPA is as fast per step as flash-attn 2 on H100 and 1.3-1.7x faster on RTX PRO 6000. TabArena 2026-09-12 run: mean train time 762 s and test inference 20 s per task (first wrapper: 930 s / 92 s); 2026-09-16 rerun median train time 57.1 s per 1K rows (66.4 s before).
speed.inference_cost_note: Self-hosted only, no API pricing. Cost is a one-time per-dataset fine-tune (minutes on one GPU); serving predictions afterwards is comparatively cheap. Lowering the prediction support cap to 8,192 (one environment variable, no retraining) removes most added prediction time at about a 2% relative-error penalty.

talent.protocol_note: TALENT main274 preset: the 300-dataset suite minus 26 TabPFN-2 / TabICLv2 development datasets = 274 (173 <=10-class classification scored by accuracy, 12 >10-class classification by accuracy, 89 regression by RMSE); one fixed 64/16/20 train/val/test split, 15 seeds, no time limit, author-default configurations; Bradley-Terry Elo anchored at RandomForest = 1,000 with 2,000-round bootstrap; scored twice under matched context policies (train-only vs train+val in-context support). Headline = train-only board; Mitra-v2 = default fine-tuned + bagged system, 0 imputed cells; TabPFN-3 and TabICLv2 keep train-only context on both boards.
talent.win_rate_vs: not reported for main274; full300 (train+val) win rate 0.891 vs TabFM 0.905 and EXAONE Tabular 0.902
talent.other: main274 train-only: TabFM 1,503.2 (rank 4.03), Mitra-v2 1,479.7 (+60/-54; rank 4.39), EXAONE Tabular 1,451.8 (4.83), TabPFN-3 1,414.8 (5.48), TabICLv2 1,399.6; train+val: TabFM 1,527.7 (3.82), EXAONE 1,519.0 (3.94), Mitra-v2 1,490.2 (+66/-60; 4.35), TabPFN-3 1,404.8 (5.78) - top three statistically indistinguishable, Mitra-v2 leads TabPFN-3 by 65-85 and TabICLv2 by 80-96 Elo. Slices (train-only / train+val): <=10-class 1,444.2 (rank 5.16) / 1,448.7 (5.18) vs TabFM 1,518.8 / 1,529.3 (Mitra-v2's weakest slice, 75-81 Elo behind); >10-class 2,070.1 (2.08) / 2,204.2 (1.58), first in the entire pool, +220 / +363 Elo over runner-up TabPFN-3 (TabFM cannot run the slice); regression 1,499.3 (3.75, highest point estimate) / 1,516.1 (3.71) vs TabFM 1,480.2 / 1,529.8 and EXAONE 1,466.7 / 1,532.6. full300 train+val: TabFM 1,516.6, EXAONE 1,510.4, Mitra-v2 1,488.6 (+69/-59; rank 4.26). Best classical baseline ModernNCA 1,166.9. Folding validation rows into the support gains Mitra-v2 0.29 accuracy points (105 of 173 datasets improve) and a 2.1% RMSE decrease (70 of 89).

other.name: TabArena overall, paper frozen 1-hour board of 2026-09-03 (51 datasets, 816 units)
other.value: Elo 1,774.6 (+95/-70), avg rank 9.02, gap-to-best 7.1%, ~9 rank-one datasets; TabFM 1,773.5 (statistical tie), EXAONE Tabular 1,749.4, AutoGluon 1.6 extreme 4h 1,742.0, TabPFN-3 1,637.5 (~137 Elo behind), TabPFN-2.6 1,583.8; only AutoGluon 1.6 (noncommercial, 4h) at 1,792.9 rates above it

other.name: TabArena classification, paper board (38 datasets, 594 units)
other.value: Elo 1,756.3 (+120/-78), avg rank 9.69, gap 9.0%; TabFM 1,755.1; ~128 Elo above TabPFN-3; Mitra-v1 in the same pool 1,350.2; mean rank 5.3 on the ten datasets with >=10k training rows vs 6.8 on the 28 smaller ones

other.name: TabArena regression, paper board (13 datasets, 222 units)
other.value: Elo 1,985.6 (+223/-134), avg rank 6.99, gap 1.5%, 3.6 outright wins of 13 (most in the pool); EXAONE Tabular 1,879.5; ~187 Elo above TabPFN-3; Mitra-v1 in the same pool 1,265.2

other.name: Mitra-v1 vs Mitra-v2 per dataset (TabArena, same frozen pool)
other.value: v2 has lower mean error on 26 of 26 classification datasets where v1 had real results (sign test p<1e-7) and 6 of 7 regression datasets; v1 required imputation on 12/38 classification and 6/13 regression datasets, v2 0%

other.name: TabArena hosted verification runs (TabArena team, 1x RTX PRO 6000)
other.value: 2026-09-12 run: Elo 1770 (position 3; binary 1746, multiclass 1826, regression 1985; normalized error 0.214), 816/816 splits, 0% imputation, 108 GPU-hours; 2026-09-16 timing rerun: 1764 (within noise). Live leaderboard row 'Mitra-v2 (default)' is joined from data/tabarena.json.

other.name: In-context support sweep (paper Sec. 3.6)
other.value: Prediction cap 512 -> 32,768 reduces error by 28% (classification) / 21% (regression) in geometric mean on the six largest datasets of each type; airline-satisfaction (87k rows) -66% of 1-AUC, SDSS17 (52k) -32% log-loss; +25% / +9% end-to-end time

differences_vs_predecessor: Mitra-v1 (arXiv 2510.21204, NeurIPS 2025; Zhang, Maddix et al.; released in AutoGluon 1.4 in July 2025) -> Mitra-v2 (2026-09-03). Same 12-layer / 512-d / 4-head element-wise 2D-attention backbone and the same <=10-class classification head (classifier parameter count unchanged at 75.7M). Changes (paper Table 1): (1) pretraining envelope: max support rows 512 -> 5,120 and query rows 128 -> 1,280 (10x context), max features 16 -> 50 (3x); (2) prior: SCM + tree priors (v1: 50% SCM / 50% tree-based, equally weighted) -> base SCM 0.35 + new Hybrid SCM 0.35 + five tree priors at 0.06 each; (3) regression head: single-output MSE -> 1,000-bin distributional cross-entropy head (+~1M params, 76.7M; the only architectural change); (4) optimizer: uniform AdamW -> Muon (2-D matrices) + AdamW hybrid with cosine schedule; (5) training run: 22,000 steps / 45M nominal tasks on 8x A100 40GB -> ~14,000 updates (regressor +3,000 fine-tuning steps) / 28.7M-34.8M nominal tasks on 4 nodes x 8 H200; (6) deployment: fine-tune + 8-fold bagging with heldout-in-support, support caps up to 32,768 rows, train-only feature reduction to a 256-feature budget, hierarchical >10-class wrapper and 16,384-row query chunks, giving 0% imputation on TabArena where v1 was imputed on 32% of classification and 46% of regression datasets (AutoGluon's stock v1 wrapper is limited to 10,000 rows / 500 features / 10 classes). Result in the same frozen TabArena pool: classification Elo 1,350.2 -> 1,756.3, regression 1,265.2 -> 1,985.6; v2 beats v1 on 26/26 classification and 6/7 regression datasets with real v1 results. The paper cautions that all changes were made at once and their individual contributions are not isolated.

notes: All numbers were checked against the arXiv HTML full text (source 2) and the mitra-finetune README (source 9). Open points: (a) total pretraining compute, GPU-hours, wall-clock and cost are not published (paper Sec. 5: 'not recoverable from the current metadata'); (b) author affiliations are not on the arXiv page - the HF card cites the report as '(Amazon, 2026)' and the TabArena wrapper lists the authors as Amazon; (c) the Hybrid SCM implementation and all synthetic generators are unreleased, so prior_code_released=false and no prior license exists; (d) the AutoGluon tutorial's limits (10,000 rows / 500 features / 10 classes) and CPU support describe AutoGluon's stock MITRA wrapper with v1 weights, not the mitra-finetune recipe behind the reported numbers; (e) TabArena config key is 'Mitra-v2_c1_default_BAG_L1', displayed as 'Mitra-v2 (default)'; 'default' means fine-tuned + 8-fold bagged, not zero-shot, and no zero-shot v2 numbers exist; (f) max_features=256 records the released feature budget (native pretraining cap is 50; wider tables are reduced, so there is no hard limit); max_samples is null because large tables are handled by support subsampling (caps 16,384-32,768) rather than a limit; (g) num_synthetic_datasets is the classifier's 28.7M nominal tasks (regressor 34.8M); (h) TabArena Elo/fit/infer values for the live leaderboard are intentionally not stored here (joined from data/tabarena.json).
